## feature

<!-- new capability this task added -->

### strand read-count columns in qc-summary

```
level: high
```

#### reason

New tests read the written Parquet and assert the split, the identity, and the zero-read case; the full suite, ruff, and pyright pass this session; an end-to-end 200k-read run shows zero identity violations.

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. `qc-summary` now writes 18 columns: `forward_reads`, `reverse_reads`, `forward_pct` join the schema right after `total_reads`.
2. The counts read the FLAG `0x10` bit (`record.is_reverse`) inside the existing single pass — no new CLI flag, no extra BAM pass.
3. Strand needs no config, so no-config runs populate the new columns (like `total_reads`/`fl`).

#### before

A user could not get forward/reverse read counts from sam-tagger at all. `samtools flagstat` reports no strand split (verified this session on a 50%-reverse BAM), and per-reference splits needed indexed `samtools view -c` queries, one per reference.

#### after

One Parquet digest answers the per-reference strand question next to `total_reads`, `fl_pct`, and the error columns.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

- `src/sam_tagger/stats/qc_summary.py:27-28` — `forward`/`reverse` fields on `_QcCounts`.
- `src/sam_tagger/stats/qc_summary.py:43-45` — the three `_SCHEMA` entries.
- `src/sam_tagger/stats/qc_summary.py:72-77` — `tally_strand` buckets by `is_reverse`.
- `src/sam_tagger/stats/qc_summary.py:118-120` — column appends; `forward_pct` guards the zero-total division.
- `src/sam_tagger/lib.py:532` — the tally call beside `qc.tally_total`.
- `tests/test_qc_summary.py:216-260` — `test_qc_summary_strand_columns` (FLAG 16, secondary 0x100, supplementary 0x800|16, unmapped excluded) and `test_qc_summary_strand_all_reverse`.

:::

## fix

None

## limitation

### no reverse_pct column

```
level: low
```

#### reason

The scope the user approved names only `forward_pct`, mirroring the existing `fl_pct` pattern, and the implementation adds exactly that column.

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. `reverse_pct` is absent by scope choice; it is derivable as `1 - forward_pct`.
2. Adding it later is one schema entry and one append.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

- `docs/plans/20261020-210605_add-qc-summary-strand-cols.plan.qmd` — the approved scope lists three columns only.

:::

## caveat

### strand counts include secondary and supplementary alignments

```
level: medium
```

#### reason

The counting loop filters only unmapped records, and a test pins a secondary (0x100) and a supplementary (0x800|16) record inside the counts; the semantics are written into the user docs.

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. `forward_reads + reverse_reads == total_reads` holds in every row — both sides count the same record set.
2. A consumer comparing against primary-only samtools counts must filter, because minimap2 emits secondary alignments by default.
3. Unmapped reads carry no strand and are excluded.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

- `tests/test_qc_summary.py:222-224` — r3 (FLAG 256) lands in `forward_reads`, r4 (FLAG 2064) in `reverse_reads`, unmapped r5 excluded from `total_reads`.
- `docs/usage.qmd:212-227` — the shipped wording on the counting semantics and the row identity.

:::

## assumption

### forward means FLAG 0x10 unset

```
level: medium
```

#### reason

The flag-bit mapping is standard SAM semantics; the operative fact for this report is that the implementation maps bit 0x10 exactly as the tests specify, and those tests pass.

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. `forward_reads` counts mapped records with FLAG `0x10` unset; `reverse_reads` counts records with the bit set.
2. The strand orientation refers to the read-to-reference alignment direction, not to library strandedness.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [statistic]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

```text
tests/test_qc_summary.py::test_qc_summary_strand_columns PASSED
  forward_reads == 2 (FLAG 0 + FLAG 256), reverse_reads == 2 (FLAG 16 + FLAG 2064)
```

:::

## conclusion

### the feature is delivered, additive, and cheap as assessed

```
level: high
```

#### reason

The full verification chain is green and the cost claim from the assessment phase is confirmed by measurement, not estimation.

#### description

```
type: [statistic]
```

1. The per-read cost measured earlier this session is ~25 ns/read (5 ms per 200k reads) for the strand branch — noise inside a BAM-decode-dominated loop.
2. The schema change is additive (15 → 18 columns); consumers selecting columns by name are unaffected.
3. An end-to-end run over a 200k-read, 100-reference BAM produced zero `forward + reverse != total_reads` violations.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [statistic]
```

## recommendation

### M: notify downstream consumers of the additive qc-summary schema

```
level: medium
```

#### reason

The schema grew 15 → 18 columns; strict-schema consumers break on additive changes too. I have not audited who those consumers are.

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. Tell qc-summary Parquet consumers about the three new columns before they upgrade.
2. The same notice still applies to the v0.3.0 `error.parquet` `to_*` columns.

#### evidence

```
level: unknown
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

None

:::

### L: prefer read-time column projection over a writer-side column-selection flag

```
level: low
```

#### reason

Demonstrated this session: `pl.read_parquet(path, columns=[...])` decodes only the named column chunks, so a configurable output schema would duplicate a capability the format already provides.

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. If a narrower view is wanted, project columns in the consuming pipeline step.
2. A writer-side `--columns` flag would fork the fixed I/O contract and the test matrix.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

- Session demo: `pl.read_parquet('/tmp/qc_demo.parquet', columns=['seq_name','total_reads','fl'])` returned a 3-column frame from a 15-column file.

:::

### L: whole-file strand counts need no sam-tagger run

```
level: low
```

#### reason

The per-reference digest is the tool's value; two global numbers are one samtools command away.

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. `samtools view -c -f 16` / `-F 16` gives the two whole-file counts directly.

#### evidence

```
level: unknown
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

None

:::
